phil-ph-01-c2.text: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy. Phenomenology. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phil-ph-01-c2.quote: every mental phenomenon, or act of consciousness, is directed toward some object
phil-ph-01-c2.claim: Husserl took from his teacher Franz Brentano the thesis that consciousness is always intentional, meaning it is always consciousness of something.

phil-ph-01-c3.text: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy. Phenomenology. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
phil-ph-01-c3.quote: (from the Greek skeptics' notion of abstaining from belief)
phil-ph-01-c3.claim: Husserl calls this move the epoché, a term borrowed from ancient Skepticism that means 'suspension'.
